# COLRv1 test fixture

`Noto-COLRv1-subset.ttf` is an 11,136-byte test-only subset of Google's
[Noto Color Emoji v2.047](https://github.com/googlefonts/noto-emoji/tree/v2.047/fonts).
The original font's SHA256 is
`23549f29b5ad741fcb4c025b8dc44652ff0f459892467ebcccec1e6bbe839b44`.
The font is licensed under SIL OFL 1.1; the unmodified upstream license is
in `OFL.txt`. This fixture is not embedded in the application.

Reproduce with fonttools:

```sh
pyftsubset Noto-COLRv1.ttf --unicodes=U+2764,U+FE0F,U+1F680,U+1F525,U+1F389,U+2705,U+1F415,U+1F308,U+1F3A8 --output-file=Noto-COLRv1-subset.ttf
```

Tests cover actual paint traversal at two sizes, gradients, clipping,
compositing, malformed input, font fallback, and BGRA upload.

`COLRProbe.ttf` is an original synthetic fixture generated by
`uv run --with fonttools python make-colr-probe.py`. It has a foreground
paint, a red/blue gradient, and SrcOut/SrcIn compositions inside a curved
clip. The same generator produces `COLRRejected.ttf`, whose valid 65-stop
paint exceeds the renderer's budget but retains a drawable base outline.
Both are test-only and use the repository's Apache-2.0 license.

The gradient midpoint is deliberately sRGB (~128), matching Chrome/Skia
and Google's same-version Noto CBDT output. CPAL specifies linear-light
interpolation (~188), but changing to that diverges from these references.
The isolated SrcOut glyph is empty in Chrome; the shared antialiased clip
is applied after composition.
